mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of over 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals a supply-side shock in a tight labor market, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase of more than 1% in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a concurrent rise in housing starts by more than 5% signals strengthening consumer demand and construction activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 1% AND HOUST > previous month + 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month while the federal funds rate remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates persistent inflation with accommodative policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month + 0.4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A steady unemployment rate below 5% for six consecutive months in conjunction with rising real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a tight labor market with robust demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 YoY > 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a month-over-month increase in RSAFS of more than 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within the following week.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS grows by more than 0.5% month-over-month.
